byChecker.summary:
Number check of CS-000 to CS-005, CS-INDEX, QR-004, QR-005, QR-009 and QR-011, plus the 14 v2 figures they reference. All 14 figure PNGs match `.hashes.json`, so none are stale.

These numbers were checked and match their sources:
- **XCR (TDS p2 and p3):** 100:41 and 2:1, 8 and 4 min pot life (150 g), 2 h 50 and 1 h 30 overcoat, 8 h 30 and 4 h 30 initial cure, about 9 h handleable, ≥9 h then 120 grit, ≥14 d, 24 h water, 15–30 °C, 20–25 °C storage, 12 months.
- **XCR SDS:** H codes, EN 166, EN ISO 374-1, EN 14387 A1, P272.
- **Ure-Bond 90 (TB):** 1A:1B and 100A:88B, 3 min mix, 8 min pot life, 4 h clamp and handling, 16 h cure, 15 min eye flush. SDS 1386A: MDI 15–35 %, CAS 101-68-8, H codes. SDS 1386B: not classified.
- **DP420 (TDS):** 20 min open time, 2.5 h handling strength at 23 °C.
- **App code:** labels.js (QR 21.4/27/14 mm, 101.6/86.6 mm rolls, 0.4 mm module, 50 copies, last ten, 47/30/3/14 budget, Q 25 % against M 15 %), core.js (EHS 24/12, 30 days), slicer.js (152.4 mm, 25.4–50.8 mm margin, 12.7 mm quantum), packer.js (3.175 mm kerf), resins.js (XCR 12 h), timeline.js slot rows, fusion.js once-per-page.
- **Other:** CS-012 dollar tiers, the 17 tensile CSVs, and the INDEX photo counts.

No number in these docs comes from a stand-in datasheet.

What fails:
- The 25 mm against 40 mm mold-label rule (R-001-30) was never settled, and it now appears in five places.
- CS-001 quotes a storage-label footer the app no longer prints.
- CS-004 leaves out the Formula Five one-hour out-gas wait (R-004-30), and it credits the team's 4 wax and 2 PVA coats to the guides.
- CS-003 §5 is missing the 45 lb grade the app plans with (R-003-31). There is no 45 lb TDS, and PBLT is not sold at 45.
- CS-003 §5 does not state the Ure-Bond TB's 30 lb/ft³ limit.
- CS-INDEX's Parent and Checked-against cells for the four in-scope QRs disagree with their headers.
- Smaller issues: an uncited tacky-tape width, a misattributed glove material, team values not labelled as team values, a contradictory ShopSabre citation, dotted cross-references that do not resolve, an arithmetic understatement in CS-003 Appendix A, and a stale QR-008 note in CS-INDEX.

I checked every number in CS-006, CS-007, CS-008, QR-001, QR-002, QR-003, QR-012 and QR-008, plus the text in figures cs006-infusion.v2, cs007-bag-stack.v2 and cs008-holds.v2. Sources were the datasheets (pdftotext), app/resins.js, app/materials.js, app/inventory.js and the SN5 source docs.

**Correct:** The IN2, West and XCR ratios, pot lives, cure figures, minimum temperatures and ratio tolerances all match the datasheets. The FEB holds match resins.js, and the bar lengths in cs008-holds are drawn to scale. The SDS H-statements and versions are right. The Ure-Bond, DP420, LiME LiNE and Ansell IPA figures match their sources. No number comes from a stand-in.

**Wrong:**
- **High: forged CF mix math (CS-008 §7 step 4, QR-001 §9).** The drafts misread R5: volume × 1.4 g/cc is the finished part's mass, not the carbon mass, and fiber is 60% of it. As written, the procedure overfills the mold about 2.25 times. The error is already in src.
- **High: the 0.5 m resin-travel rule is cited to the wrong document.** It is credited to R7, but it actually comes from `SN5 Composites/Composites Info & Safety.docx`, which CS-006 never cites.
- **Medium:**
  - The 20–30 min infusion time is given for small parts; the source says it is for larger pieces.
  - "IN2 vapor pressure is low" has no source; every SDS in the file says "not determined".
  - The TDS gives two FAST pot-life figures (9–14 min in the text, 10–14 in the table), and the drafts quote only 10–14 without noting the 9–14 text figure.
  - R-008-31 ("after the weekend") is not applied in CS-008, QR-001 or the cs008-holds figure.
  - R-006-30 is not applied: CS-006 still says the shop stocks OV/P100, but the restock row says A + P100.
  - The Ansell 93-800 glove is a latex/neoprene/nitrile blend, not nitrile, and its acetone breakthrough is 17 min under ASTM F739, not only the 21 min EN figure (QR-008, and the parent CS-009).
- **Low:**
  - The Airtac flash point comes from the 2005 MSDS of the predecessor product.
  - 25 °C is attached to the 80–100 min SLOW figure, which the datasheet gives no temperature for.
  - Several team numbers are not labelled as team rules or cited: 27/25 inHg, the 1 and 2 inHg drop tests, the 0.65 and 0.9 mix factors, 30–50 mm, 300–400 mm, ±10% and ≥2 min.
  - CS-007 §6 leaves out H302 and H312.

Key files: `02 CS Standards/overhaul/drafts/CS-008.md`, `CS-006.md`, `QR-001.md`, `QR-002.md`, `QR-008.md`, `02 CS Standards/src/figures/cs008-holds.v2.svg`, `SN5 Composites/Documentation/Forged_Compression Molded Carbon Fiber.docx`, `SN5 Composites/Composites Info & Safety.docx`.

Shop review in the simon persona of §6 Safety and §7 Procedure in CS-000 to CS-014 and all 15 QRs, checked against STYLE.md, REGISTER.md (including the Answers, Round 2, Round 3 and Round 4 sections), app code and the datasheets (pdftotext; no numbers taken from stand-ins). The problems are on the shop floor, and some of them would cost a part or a mold:
- Two drop-test steps. Nothing says to reopen the valve after the drop test, and that matters most on an overnight wet layup. No document says the gauge has to sit on the bag side of the valve. Only the figure shows it.
- An IPA wipe goes onto a mold that has already been released (CS-006 §7.2, QR-002).
- A mold stays at "Ready for layup" after a part is pulled, and nobody is told to update Parts pulled.
- Engraving the back face "before releasing the vacuum" can't be done, because the back face is lying on the table.
- The tacky tape is placed "½ in off the part", which would put it inside the inlet spiral on the flange.
- Four Round 3 and 4 register rows were never applied: R-004-30 (the 1 h wax-to-PVA wait), R-001-17 (marking blanks, which Simon answered), R-001-30 and R-011-31. R-006-30, R-008-30 and R-008-31 were not applied either.

- No eye protection is stated in CS-007 §6 or CS-005 §6.
- There is no handling rule for IN2's H360F (fertility).
- Ure-Bond's PPE line has the wrong glove source and no rule for asthma or a past reaction. Its respirator is still a "should" even though the shop stocks one.
- Gloves go on only after the solvent wipe in the bond prep.
- The DP420 load hold before an insert takes load is a bare placeholder, with no interim number.

Rubric (persona): Accuracy 4, Feasibility 4, Actionability 3, Completeness 3, Consistency 3, Style 4. Average 3.5, so REVISE. Steve's notes and catalog-categories.json passed the safety check (PPE products all classify as safety-ppe). The one nit is that the CNC/tooling-board row pushes waxes.

The real risks sit in the wiring and in the product blurbs the tool hands back, and they would hurt a part, a mold or a person. (2) STEVE_SYSTEM rule 3 never got the R-STV-01 no-go list, and its own \"Fibreglast mixing kit\" example searches straight to a polyester and MEKP repair kit. (3) The PVA handle's blurb gives a wax coat count below CS-004's 4-coat minimum, and steveGuard does not catch \"layers\". (4) The EZ Mix Containers blurb tells the reader to mix by volume, while CS-008 requires weighing IN2 and XCR. (5) BPO Hardener and the resin kits slip past the category exclusions. (6) Nothing stops Steve selling a resin or adhesive in place of the team's. (7) The CNC topic pushes only wax. Smaller items: Compoflex is a stack-replacement product and is framed in a slightly disparaging way, QR-010's \"never act on a number from Steve\" is too narrow, the README makes untrue claims about search_steve_notes and the guard, the rule 2 example handle is wrong, \"one product\" appears at fibreglast-lines.md:41, and REGISTER's Steve table is stale against R-STV-07.

needsHuman.where: §7.5 step 4; CS-001.md §7.4 item 2; QR-005.md §2 step 2; revision row D
needsHuman.note: The defect is real. The back face sits on the vacuum table, so it cannot be engraved in the machining setup (the error dates from src Rev D). Neither proposed fix holds up as written, though. (a) A 3-axis router cannot engrave text on a vertical side face. (b) Flipping a finished mold puts its contoured working surface on the spoilboard, which will not hold under vacuum and risks the surface. My recommendation: engrave the flat back face of the glued blank in a short first setup, with its own Z zero, before it is flipped for the working-surface program. This adds a setup and a Z zero, which affects RFS time and the Z-zero risk §7.4 warns about, so it is a lead's method call. It has to be written the same way in CS-005 §7.5, CS-001 §7.4 item 2, QR-005 §2, cs001-mold-identity and a history line.
